brief.prompt: Create one complete 16:9 handmade paper/card diorama thumbnail for a historical London cost-of-living investigation. First glance: one oversized silver-colored wage coin under a rising paper wage ribbon, while a small but clearly recognizable bread-and-fuel basket is pushed farther beyond it, making the counterintuitive question visible. Use a bold low camera angle, physical layered edges and a strong warm/cool light split; direct attention from the rising ribbon down to the basket with a cut-paper diagonal. Include the exact large rounded paper lettering: ‘MORE PAY. LESS BUY.’ Keep only bread, a fuel bundle and a candle as supporting necessities. Rich tactile fibers, thickness, folds and contact shadows; no glossy CGI, modern coinage, modern prices, charts, logos, realistic documentary photo, or implied exact household bills. The metaphor must read as a model of relative purchasing power, not a literal event. Thumbnail QA title context: ‘When Wages Rose, Why Did the Basics Cost More?’ At 320×180 the coin, upward ribbon, basket and words must remain immediately legible.
brief.visual_intent: A price-versus-wage reversal: the gaze travels from the rising wage ribbon to the basket that remains costly relative to it. Verify the relationship and exact title at 320×180; the text is a separate concise hook.
